In an autonomous AI network, Sybil resistance can be enforced via cryptoeconomic staking where every agent must lock native tokens to publish data, effectively
 creating a digital island of verified compute. If an attacker attempts to spawn fake identities to hollow out consensus, slashing protocols instantly confiscate their staked collateral. This transforms the network atlas into a secure topology where identity generation carries a strict, prohibitive financial cost proportional to the volume of nodes deployed.
